style.description: Short human-readable illustration style label, e.g. 'soft watercolor, pastel palette'. Used in prose (image_prompts mention it) and as a quick summary; the paid scripts inject 'style_guide' (required) into every API call, not this field.

style_guide.description: REQUIRED structured style guide. The render and stylesheet scripts assemble a single deterministic style block from these fields (in fixed order: medium → palette → line → lighting → mood) and inject it byte-identically into every API call. This locks book-wide visual consistency — each page is a separate stateless API call, and having the exact same verbatim block in every prompt is the documented consistency mechanism (per Google's Book_illustration workflow). Both paid scripts refuse to run when this object is missing or empty. At least one field must be set.

medium.description: Rendering medium and technique, e.g. 'soft watercolor with pen-and-ink outline'.

palette.description: 3–5 named or hex color swatches that define the book's palette, e.g. ['warm cream #F5E9D4', 'sage green #8FAF85', 'dusty coral #E8917A']. These are injected verbatim — the more specific, the better the cross-page consistency.

line.description: Line-work description, e.g. 'thin sepia ink, even weight, rounded corners'.

lighting.description: Lighting direction, quality, and color temperature, e.g. 'golden-hour side-light, soft warm shadows, no harsh edges'.

mood.description: Overall mood and rendering vocabulary, e.g. 'cozy, gentle, storybook calm, slightly naive brushwork'.

characters.description: Explicit cast. ONE entry per REAL character in the story. Drives the style sheet — the style sheet shows exactly these characters and no others. Never rely on auto-extraction from prose.

name.description: Character name exactly as written in image_prompts

appearance.description: Concrete visual description: species, age, hair, ONE specific outfit/clothing, colours, distinguishing features. The outfit named here becomes the character's canonical outfit locked into the style sheet and worn unchanged on every page — name exactly one outfit. More specific = more consistent across pages.

ref_image.description: Optional reference photo(s) for THIS character: a single absolute path, or an array of paths. EVERY referenced image must show ONLY this character — single-person images only. If a source photo contains multiple people, crop it first with scripts/crop_character.py and point ref_image at the per-person crop; never reference the multi-person original. Used for face and hair likeness only; clothing/outfit always comes from 'appearance', not from these photos. Capped at 5 (Gemini 3 Pro Image character-lane limit used by make_style_sheet.py). Crops compose with the array form: e.g. ['ref-mia.png', '/photos/mia-solo.jpg'] (a Stage-1 crop plus a solo photo of the same person). Mapped to this character only — there is no shared global pool.

style_sheet.description: Path to this character's generated style sheet PNG (filled in by make_style_sheet.py). Used by render_book.py to select per-page reference images.

text_mode.description: How page text is rendered. 'native' (default): ask the image model to render the story text directly into the illustration (output goes to page-NN-native.png). 'overlay': generate image with a text-safe zone, then Pillow-composite text via overlay_text.py. 'long': each body page becomes two physical pages — (1) full-bleed art with no text (pages/page-NN-long.png), (2) a separate text-only page with the story text on a centered, feathered semi-transparent panel over a blurred/washed copy of the art (pages/page-NN-long-text.png). Cover (page 1) stays a single combined overlay-style page. Default cost = same as other modes (1 paid call per logical page); pages with optional 'text_background_prompt' add 1 extra paid call for a dedicated text-page background. render_book.py's --text-mode flag overrides this per run.

language.description: Optional BCP-47 language tag for the book text (e.g. 'en', 'de', 'en-GB'). Used as dc:language metadata in EPUB output. Default: 'en'.

fonts.description: Optional book-wide map of text role -> font family name. Defines which font each per-page 'font' role uses. Values are family names (e.g. 'Arial', 'Patrick Hand') resolved at render time: bundled asset in assets/fonts/ -> system-installed font -> bundled role default. Omit to use the bundled Andika (reader) / PatrickHand (display).

display.description: Title/cover font family. Default: Patrick Hand (bundled).

resolution.description: Optional book-wide image resolution for page rendering. 2K (default) is good for screen and print up to ~8×8 in; 1K is faster/cheaper for drafts; 4K for large-format print. The render CLI --resolution flag overrides this value when passed explicitly.

aspect_ratio.description: Optional book-wide aspect ratio applied to both style sheets and page renders. When omitted, the model picks framing on each call (non-deterministic). Set this to lock consistent framing across all sheets and pages (e.g. '4:3' for landscape, '3:4' for portrait, '1:1' for square). The stylesheet/render CLI --aspect-ratio flag overrides this value when passed explicitly.

saved_formats.description: Optional list of book file formats assembled after a full render: 'pdf' (multi-page PDF) and/or 'epub' (fixed-layout EPUB3). When omitted, ALL formats are produced. An empty array skips assembly. The render CLI --saved-formats flag overrides this value when passed explicitly ('none' to skip for one run).

characters.description: Names of the characters appearing on this page. MUST match characters[].name exactly. Drives which per-character style sheets are sent as references when rendering this page. Use an empty array [] for wordless or character-free pages.

text.description: Story text for this page/spread. Empty string for cover or wordless pages.

image_prompt.description: Full image generation prompt. Must name characters and mention style. Content only — do not include text-position or safe-zone directives; the render script appends those transparently from text_placement.

text_placement.description: Where text lands on the image. 'floating' (default, native mode only): the image model picks the most visually pleasing placement; the overlay path degrades this to 'bottom'. 'top'/'bottom': pin text to a fixed band.

text_color_hint.description: Optional hint for text color, e.g. 'dark' or 'light'. Default: dark.

text_align.description: Horizontal alignment of the overlay text. Default: left. Use 'center' for cover/title pages.

font.description: Font for the text overlay. 'reader' (Andika, body text) or 'display' (PatrickHand, titles/cover). Default: reader.

text_background_prompt.description: Long mode only. When set, generates a dedicated background image for this page's text page via ONE extra paid Gemini call (the book style block is injected; no character references are sent). Omit to derive the background from this page's own illustration — blurred and lightened — at no extra cost. Ignored in overlay/native modes and on the cover or empty-text pages. If set on an empty-text page a warning is logged and no text page is generated.
